draft.title: Persons and environment
card: an individual with a unique identity. Each person has their own experiences, beliefs and ways of seeing the world.
the natural and built world that people live in. It includes land, climate and water, as well as buildings, towns and roads.
People are shaped by their environment. A child raised in a remote farming town and a child raised in a busy city can develop different habits, skills and outlooks.
The link runs both ways. People also change their environment, for example by clearing land, building homes or planting gardens.
draft.remember: People shape their environment, and their environment shapes them.

a.q: Which of these is part of the built environment?
opts: A suburban shopping centre
A coastal sand dune
A river running through a valley
A rainforest in northern Queensland
a.why: The built environment is made by people, and a shopping centre is built. The dune, river and rainforest are natural, so they belong to the natural environment.

b.q: Priya grew up in a small fishing town in Tasmania. She now lives in Sydney and takes up cycling to work. Which statement best describes the link between Priya and her environment?
opts: Her surroundings shape her habits, and her choices affect them
Her surroundings decide her habits, and she cannot change them
She shapes her surroundings, but they do not shape her
Her identity is the same as her surroundings in each place
b.why: Her town and city shape her habits, and her choices, such as cycling, also affect her surroundings. The option saying surroundings decide everything is wrong because it leaves out the influence a person has. The card says people are shaped by their environment and also change it.
b.clue: The link between a person and the environment runs both ways.

proposal.title: Persons and environment
card: an individual with a unique identity. Each person has their own experiences, beliefs and ways of seeing the world.
the natural and built world that people live in. It includes land, climate and water, as well as buildings, towns and roads.
People are shaped by their environment. A child raised in a remote farming town and a child raised in a busy city can develop different habits, skills and outlooks.
The link runs both ways. People also change their environment, for example by clearing land, building homes or planting gardens.
proposal.remember: People shape their environment, and their environment shapes them.

a.q: Which example shows the environment shaping a person?
opts: A teen in a beach town takes up surfing
A family plants a garden in their backyard
A council builds a new road through a suburb
A farmer clears bushland to grow wheat crops
a.why: Living near the beach influences the teen's habits and skills, so the place is shaping the person. The garden, road and cleared bushland are all people changing their environment, which is the other direction of the link.
a.clue: In each case, ask who or what is doing the changing.

b.q: Priya grew up in a Tasmanian fishing town, where she learned to swim and fish. Now in Sydney, she helps plant trees along a local creek. What does this show?
opts: Her surroundings shaped her, and she also changes them
Her surroundings shaped her, so she cannot change them
She changes her surroundings, but they did not shape her
Only her new city shapes her, not the town she grew up in
b.why: Her fishing town shaped her skills, and planting trees along the creek changes her new surroundings. Saying only Sydney shapes her is tempting because it is where she lives now, but it ignores the skills her home town gave her.
b.clue: Look at what Priya learned as a child and what she does in Sydney.
